definitions.explanation: A simple sugar (monosaccharide) found naturally in fruits, honey, and some vegetables. It is one of the sweetest natural sugars and is widely used in the food industry.

examples.japanese: ⟦{果物|くだもの}→果物：00509_kudamono⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{果糖|かとう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{含|ふく}まれている→含む：01982_fukumu⟧。
{果糖|かとう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{砂糖|さとう}→砂糖：00884_satou⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{甘|あま}み→甘み：17244_amami⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{強|つよ}い→強い：00820_tsuyoi⟧。
examples.english: Fructose is sweeter than table sugar.

examples.japanese: ⟦{清涼飲料水|せいりょういんりょうすい}→清涼飲料水：17030_seiryouinryousui⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{使|つか}われる→使う：00473_tsukau⟧{果糖|かとう}ブドウ{糖液糖|とうえきとう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{摂取量|せっしゅりょう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{注意|ちゅうい}→注意：01464_chuui⟧⟦しましょう→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Be careful about your intake of high-fructose corn syrup used in soft drinks.

notes:
Compound of {果|か} ('fruit') and {糖|とう} ('sugar'). The term literally means 'fruit sugar,' reflecting the natural source of this monosaccharide. Essential vocabulary for reading food labels, nutrition information, and health-related articles in Japanese.

USAGE:
Appears frequently on ingredient lists, in health and diet discussions, and in science education. The compound {果糖|かとう}ブドウ{糖液糖|とうえきとう} ('high-fructose corn syrup') is one of the most commonly seen terms on Japanese food packaging.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {果糖|かとう}ブドウ{糖液糖|とうえきとう}: high-fructose corn syrup
- {果糖|かとう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{含|ふく}まれる→含む：01982_fukumu⟧: to contain fructose
- {果糖|かとう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{摂取|せっしゅ}→摂取：09322_sesshu⟧: fructose intake
- {果糖|かとう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{甘|あま}み→甘み：17244_amami⟧: the sweetness of fructose

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{加糖|かとう}→加糖：20005_katou⟧: sweetened; sugar-added — homophone with different kanji; means adding sugar to something
- ブドウ{糖|とう}: glucose — the other common simple sugar; often paired with {果糖|かとう}
- ⟦{砂糖|さとう}→砂糖：00884_satou⟧: sugar — the general everyday word for table sugar (sucrose)
- ⟦{糖分|とうぶん}→糖分：15847_toubun⟧: sugar content — refers to the total amount of sugar in food
